subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Wireless Power Transfer
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Wireless Power Transfer.

hook.text: Wireless charging sends power through air using magnetic fields — no plugs, no wear, no sparks.

buildup.text: A transmitter coil creates an alternating magnetic field. A receiver coil captures it and converts to DC.

discovery.text: Resonant coupling boosts efficiency — both coils tuned to the same frequency transfer energy more effectively.

twist.text: Distance kills efficiency. At 10 cm gap, efficiency drops below 80%. Metal objects in between absorb energy as heat.

climax.text: Phone pads, electric toothbrushes, and even electric bus charging systems use wireless power.

punchline.text: Magnetic field across the gap — wireless trades efficiency for convenience.

quiz.question: Why does resonant coupling improve wireless power transfer efficiency?
options: It increases the transmitted power level
Tuning both coils to the same frequency maximizes energy transfer between them
It eliminates the need for a receiver coil
